Regional ILI Forecasting Demo: Persistence, Ridge, Gradient Boosting, and LSTM

Completed retrospective demo using revised historical ILINet data. CPU, fixed seed 2026. No live forecasting, probabilistic calibration, or significance claims.

Research question and data

Can a small pooled LSTM improve two-observation-week-ahead regional weighted ILI predictions over persistence, regularized linear regression, and gradient boosting?

CDC ILINet data provided by CMU Delphi: 4,690 rows, ten HHS regions, 469 consecutive CDC/MMWR weeks per region (2010w40–2019w39). wili is weighted ILI outpatient visit percentage: 2.5 means 2.5%; error units are percentage points. This is neither laboratory-confirmed influenza nor population infection prevalence.

Time split and information restrictions

Each sample uses 12 consecutive regional observations ending at origin and targets origin + 14 days. Both origin and target must belong to one split. Earlier-split history may be used; the last two origins before a boundary are excluded. Week 53 is retained. Test includes two continuous seasons; later Test inputs can use earlier observed Test values, without refitting.

The global scaler uses 3130 unique Train region-week observations, mean 1.57999623, population SD 1.23860648. It transforms histories and training targets only; one-hot and calendar features remain unchanged. Ridge/tree receive 24 features; LSTM receives a 12×1 sequence and the same 12 static features. Annual sine/cosine use target-date days since 2000-01-01 divided by 365.2425.

Models and selection

Persistence copies the last raw observation. All learned models are pooled across regions and fitted only on Train. No Train+Validation refit. Ridge uses validation region-equal MAE and larger alpha on exact ties. The fixed tree has no internal early stopping. The LSTM resets hidden state per window, uses an LSTM(1,16) and a linear head on hidden state plus static features, MSE/Adam, shuffled Train batches, gradient clipping and validation-only stopping. No Test labels enter training or selection.

Validation and Test results

Macro-MAE averages regional MAEs equally. Pooled MAE/RMSE weight samples equally. Improvement (%) = 100 × (Persistence Macro-MAE − model Macro-MAE) / Persistence Macro-MAE. A zero baseline yields NA. All four models share 500 Validation and 1,020 Test samples. Each model is fitted using 3,000 Train windows; Train is not a held-out evaluation set. Predictions are never clipped.

Test overall all Persistence 1020 0.490299 0.490299 0.850343 0.000000 0 percentage points
Test overall all Ridge 1020 0.417382 0.417382 0.778048 14.871951 0 percentage points
Test overall all HGB 1020 0.431142 0.431142 0.911869 12.065437 0 percentage points
Test overall all LSTM 1020 0.435714 0.435714 0.848319 11.132942 0 percentage points

The lowest Test Macro-MAE was obtained by Ridge. LSTM Test Macro-MAE was lower than Persistence (0.4357 versus 0.4903 percentage points; improvement 11.13%). This is a descriptive comparison in one fixed historical split. Validation MAE was 0.7458 at epoch 1 and 0.3089 at the final epoch. The restored epoch was 21 of 29. Training MSE changed from 0.8435 to 0.1339. The curve documents optimization and validation selection, but does not by itself identify why a model generalizes differently. The small fixed architecture, training objective, and seasonal differences are possible factors, not tested explanations.

Checks and limitations

Automated checks cover CDC week 53, horizon, boundary membership, legal history crossing, bad panel rejection, train-only scaling, prediction keys, manual metrics, CSV metric reconstruction, label perturbation, and model reload agreement (absolute tolerance 1e−6). See run_summary.json and execution_log.txt for actual evidence.

  • Historical values are revisions retrieved now; this is not a real-time vintage backtest. The horizon begins at the last observed week, not a verified publication date.
  • Regions and adjacent windows are dependent. No window-independent significance tests were performed.
  • Only 2010–2019, one split, and one seed are examined; conclusions need not apply after the pandemic.
  • This is continuous point forecasting. AUROC/AUPRC are inapplicable; course discrimination/calibration requirements still need an appropriate study design, without arbitrary dichotomization.
  • No prediction intervals, peak alerts, extra covariates, or additional hyperparameter searches were introduced.

Reproduction and assistance

Use the included locked requirements, raw snapshot and README commands. Models are saved locally. Codex implemented, debugged, ran, checked and documented this demo; record that assistance according to course rules if used in a course project.

Next discussion: real-time data availability and vintage design; an appropriate regression discrimination/calibration design; robustness across seasons or seeds under a new pre-specified protocol.
